audit.why: MC_REAL_GAMES has 1754 games at 50.06%. The lane shape is genuine: Ziggs has one escape on a 20s cooldown and must stand still to cast, so Fizz reaches him whenever the satchel is spent.

Both layers and the packet levelChart agree on seven Fizz rows, so nothing was moved. The spike shape is real: Urchin Strike falls to 6s and Playful/Trickster to 8s while Hexplosive Minefield stays a flat 16s at every rank, so Fizz's tempo advantage widens with levels.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and mid both say Fizz's R 'adds a stun'. Chum the Waters is a knockup, not a stun. early credits the no-collision passive with letting you 'walk through his Q bombs' — the passive moves through units, not through skillshots. wants.you[0] calls E 'no-collision' and wants.you[2] has E dodging his 'W hop-away', which is not a thing that can be dodged. breakdown.cooldowns holds no number (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Kit: Fizz R is flagged knockup. Fizz P is 'can move through units'. Fizz E is untargetable and grounds. Ziggs W Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s at 1000 range, knocks enemies away and Ziggs himself; Q Bouncing Bomb 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s at 850; E Hexplosive Minefield a flat 16s at every rank, slowing on contact; R Mega Inferno Bomb 120/95/70s at 5000 range.
audit.corrected: Knockup named correctly, the passive's real effect stated, and the mine-slow-into-bomb sequence written into the trade lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells you that raw resistances are the wrong purchase into Ziggs.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is flagged percentHealth, so stacking armour or MR does not reduce it proportionally.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentions that Short Fuse is an auto-attack reset, so a reader watches for the ability cast instead of the wind-up.
audit.why: Ziggs P is flagged autoReset and its cooldown shortens every time he casts, so the empowered auto is the reliable opener tell.
audit.corrected: Written into early, ahead and dontsFull[2].d.

edits.before: From level 1 you're heavily favored: your no-collision passive lets you walk through his Q bombs, and your Q-E gap close lands before he can kite away with his short W hop. Ziggs has no real answer to a committed dash — he only has Satchel Charge to create space, and once that's on cooldown he's dead weight in melee range. Punish him every time he pushes the wave to poke, since he has to stand still to cast.
edits.after: From level 1 you're favoured: your passive walks you through the wave so his minions never body-block the approach, and Urchin Strike lands before he can satchel away. Ziggs has no real answer to a committed dash — Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and is the only space he can make — and once it is spent he is dead weight in melee range. His Short Fuse auto is the wind-up tell; punish the moment it fires.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 you keep snowballing the lane: your all-in only gets faster and higher-damage as Q/E cooldowns shrink, and once you hit 6 your R fish adds a stun that guarantees the kill if he tries to disengage. Ziggs' ultimate is mostly useful for sieging or executing from afar, not for winning 1v1s against a diving assassin, so his power spike doesn't flip lane the way it does versus ranged foes.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 you keep snowballing: Urchin Strike falls to 6s and Playful/Trickster to 8s while his minefield stays a flat 16s at every rank, and at 6 your fish knocks him up, which beats the satchel he wants to leave on. Mega Inferno Bomb is a 5000-range siege tool, not a 1v1 answer to a diving assassin, so his level 6 doesn't flip the lane the way it does against ranged laners.

notes:
The packet suspectName on wants.foe[1] 'Land Satchel Charge' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Satchel Charge is the correct W name and the line is fine as written. DEFER CHECK: packet.games and the brief's top-level games both read 1754, so this matchup was audited normally. One thing I could not resolve from the kits and am flagging rather than changing: the chart gives Fizz all seven rows and the page rates the lane FAVOURED 4/10, but the win rate is 50.06% over 1754 games, which is dead even. I did not move any row, because nothing in either kit tells me which stage the chart is overstating — a stale row is safer than a row that argues with itself. If the user wants it reconciled, the likely candidates are the two late rows where Mega Inferno Bomb's 5000-range siege pressure stops being a lane consideration. Hexplosive Minefield's flat 16s at every rank is unusual and is now used as the concrete tempo argument in mid.
